AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli.title: The Jacobian challenge (Christian Merten's AG version), Part II: abelian schemes and arithmetic moduli
AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli.reason: Extend the immutable field-level abelian-variety/Picard foundation to actual abelian schemes over general bases. Also import the unchanged ModularCurves relative elliptic specializations. Preserve dimension-general relative duality, quotient, realization, Serre-Tate, complex-family and arithmetic Hom results; no new competing polarized-moduli stack is constructed.

FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeThe.title: Modular curves, following Katz–Mazur, Part II: finite flat groups and integral p-adic Hodge theory
FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeThe.reason: Start beyond the actual finite-group and elliptic p-divisible/Serre-Tate branch of the unchanged anchor, not beyond an assumed general Dieudonne classification. Import its general Cartier duality and henselian connected-etale theorem. Add arbitrary-height p-divisible groups, integral classification, deformation, residual-type and ramification theory with all small-prime and coefficient restrictions.

AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A0.reason: Retain the import/reexport boundary for R09.1-R09.6 and A0-extension, not a second general representability, cohomology or Artin construction. Make the README-declared exports to A1 and A2 explicit. R09.7 resolution and later arithmetic moduli are not new prerequisites.

AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A1.keeps: Construct the dimension-general proper smooth group scheme over S with geometrically connected fibres and locally constant relative dimension. Retain relative rigidity including nonreduced bases, commutativity, translation-invariant differentials, square/cube, homomorphisms versus arbitrary maps, the map-as-homomorphism-plus-translation theorem under its hypotheses, products and arbitrary base change. Import the existing field-level abelian-variety carrier and structural results, and the relative elliptic Weierstrass/group-law and square/cube specializations. Prove actual equivalences on the field and relative-dimension-one cases preserving their group laws, differential bundles and functorial operations; do not infer equality of morphisms merely from geometric fibres or choose a global polarization in the definition.
AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A1.reason: The anchors own the field carrier and the genus-one construction. They do not supply the higher-dimensional relative/nonreduced-base rigidity theorem. Import specializations and prove compatibility rather than reconstructing the existing elliptic object.

AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A2.keeps: Apply A0 to the relative Picard degree-zero algebraic space and prove the abelian-space-to-scheme theorem with the actual Faltings-Chai I.1.9 base hypotheses. Retain the resulting dimension-general relative dual, rigidified Poincare bundle, biduality, independence of an auxiliary ample bundle where used, phi_L and its tensor/translation/pullback identities, polarizations, symmetric homomorphisms, Rosati involutions and polarization types. Import the curve/field Picard and field dual objects and the relative elliptic Picard/Poincare and dual-comparison package. Prove scheme- and pairing-compatible specialization, including the rigidifying base-line correction and the chosen translation sign in the elliptic principal polarization. Neither proper algebraic space implies scheme nor local existence of a polarization is an assumed substitute for the required theorem.
AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A2.reason: Field-valued Picard/Jacobian and relative elliptic duality are existing work; general-base dual representability and its compatible evaluation pairing remain new. No theorem of curve Picard representability is silently generalized in dimension.

AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3.keeps: Construct the actual nonaffine fppf quotient abelian scheme by a finite locally free subgroup, with universal property, effective descent, flat quotient map and arbitrary base change under the proved hypotheses. Retain isogenies and their relative duals and all comparisons. Prove [n] and its torsion kernel finite locally free of rank n^(2g) for n nonzero on each dimension-g component. State the etaleness/invertibility criterion on the positive-dimensional locus and handle the zero-dimensional identity separately. Import the anchor field multiplication/isogeny results and relative elliptic 2A-2E specializations, and use the generic finite-group, Cartier, affine-quotient and descent suppliers only in their actual domains. Retain the general Weil pairing A[n] by A-dual[n] into mu_n, the polarization-induced alternating form and its precise radical/perfectness criterion, and Tate-module pairings with their twist and permitted coefficient primes. Neither p-primary torsion nor a non-etale pairing is replaced by geometric points; a nonprincipal polarization does not give an automatic perfect self-pairing.
AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3.reason: Cartier duality is canonically owned by ModularCurves 0B and reexported by R07.1. Generic affine quotient existence is not the nonaffine abelian quotient theorem. All relative higher-dimensional construction, dimension-dependent ranks and pairing compatibilities are retained.

AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A4.keeps: Retain actual relative H1_dR, its Hodge exact sequence, Gauss-Manin connection, cup pairing and base change; the etale Tate-module local system for ell invertible on S; and integral complex-homology/de Rham comparisons. Construct the general abelian-scheme Serre-Tate equivalence on objects and morphisms, including endomorphism/polarization lifting conditions and effectivity. The early Serre-Tate prefix uses finite torsion and the common p-divisible category, before the later Hodge-filtration/tangent calculation. Import R07.1 p-divisible/duality data, R07.2 Dieudonne and the consolidated generic Grothendieck-Messing theorem, and R07.6 only for its additional local tangent/obstruction/model comparisons. Import the unchanged elliptic 7E/7F package and prove compatibility without making that anchor depend on A4. Preserve the exact nilpotent-base versus nilpotent-PD hypotheses, all relative realization maps, and the structured tangent comparison; do not replace an equivalence of deformation categories by a bijection of isomorphism classes.
AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A4.reason: The generic p-divisible deformation equivalence is consolidated at R07.2 rather than reproved here or made to depend on its later R07.6 application. The field/elliptic specializations and the general structured Serre-Tate theorem are distinct targets. Reject the evidence suggestion to make immutable 7F consume A4.

AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A5.keeps: Retain Riemann bilinear relations, algebraicity of polarized complex tori, the equivalence with polarizable integral homological Hodge structures of types (-1,0) and (0,-1), and the relative analytic polarized-family/variation theorem on the existing lattice and analytic carriers. Retain the comparison from an algebraic abelian scheme to its analytic variation, the actual Siegel universal family, monodromy and symplectic level maps. Import the existing genus-one lattice-to-elliptic uniformization from R12.1 and identify this specialization with the unchanged elliptic scheme, invariant differential and Weil pairing. Prove the polarization, homology/cohomology, dual-lattice and sign comparisons. No converse algebraization over an algebraic base is used here: that remains V5 after PEL M3, and no arbitrary integral lattice is assumed unimodular.
AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A5.reason: R12.1 already owns genus-one analytic uniformization; A5 adds the polarized dimension-general and analytic-family comparison. Retaining the early analytic branch avoids an A5-M3-V5 cycle.

AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6.keeps: Extend the existing field Hom/End API with finite generation and torsion freeness, Poincare complete reducibility, semisimplicity of the rational endomorphism algebra, Rosati positivity, polarized-isogeny degree formulas and compatibility with relative duality/geometric fibres. Import the general Weil-restriction functor, algebraic-space representability for finite locally free bases and its base-change maps from R09.3. Prove the extra finite-etale preservation of abelian schemes by split-product descent and the actual A2 scheme criterion; do not infer properness from finite local freeness alone. Retain the finite-separable-field Galois-equivariant Tate-module induction comparison, embedding-choice independence, and the dual-number tangent-bundle counterexample. Keep arithmetic moduli/Hodge-line exports on the actual PEL/Hilbert objects, not a second moduli construction, and do not infer good reduction at a ramified integral place from the field-level induction formula.
AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6.reason: The anchor supplies basic Hom/End but not the arithmetic finiteness, semisimplicity or positivity theorems. General restriction-of-scalars representability is an existing supplier; preservation and the arithmetic comparison remain A6 theorems.

FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeThe.keeps: Use the unchanged general finite locally free commutative group-scheme and Cartier-duality carrier, affine finite quotient/torsor theorem and effective descent of 0B/0C/0E. Import 7E PD-2 for the finite-level connected-etale sequence over henselian local rings and its actual base-change/special-fibre splitting statement, and PD-1 for the elliptic tower. Construct the genuinely new arbitrary-height p-divisible category and coherent towers with ranks p^(nh), exact multiplication transitions, duality, morphisms, inverse-limit Tate modules and their topology in the permitted generic-fibre regime. Prove the tower-level connected-etale and base-change comparisons without assuming the entire henselian lift splits. Retain flat-closure/subgroup/model conditions, Raynaud mixed-characteristic e < p-1 uniqueness and full faithfulness with flat kernel/cokernel and Ext injectivity, the specified (p,...,p)/F-vector-scheme classification and tame-inertia calculations. Preserve finite presentation and all source ramification hypotheses; the strict inequality supplies no unrestricted dyadic substitute. Retain multiplicative, constant, ordinary-nonsplit, supersingular and distinct-integral-model tests.
FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeThe.reason: Contrary to an audit lead, 0B is already general Cartier duality, and 7E PD-2 is already the general henselian finite-group theorem, not only an elliptic statement. Arbitrary-height towers and integral local classification go beyond those anchors.

FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeThe.keeps: Construct the actual Dieudonne module/crystal of finite flat and p-divisible groups over the source perfect bases, fixing covariance, F/V and semilinear linearization conventions. Retain integral classification, exactness, duality, height/dimension formulas, ordinary/supersingular and isogeny comparisons, and the descent/forms work not covered by algebraically closed classification. Import CR.0/CR.1 PD/crystal carriers and the independent VB0 rational isocrystal carrier, standard blocks and Dieudonne-Manin slope theorem in their stated field/coefficient scope; prove agreement after rationalizing the integral functor. Import 7E only for its elliptic Frobenius/Verschiebung and height-one/two specializations. Consolidate here the general Grothendieck-Messing equivalence for p-divisible lifts and admissible Hodge-filtration lifts over the exact nilpotent-PD thickenings of the selected source, with all morphisms, Cartier-dual and coefficient compatibilities and effectivity; tensor operations are used only on the appropriate crystal/isocrystal objects or in separately proved tensor-structured cases; this realizes the existing R07.2 deformation target using the generic proof formerly also assigned in R07.6. Ordinary ideal nilpotence, divided-power nilpotence and nilpotence of p are not interchangeable. Retain every small-prime exception and source-qualified extension rather than asserting the equivalence for arbitrary thickenings.
FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeThe.reason: Keep the integral group/crystal functor and generic deformation theorem in the foundational R07.2 scope. Reuse, rather than duplicate, rational Dieudonne-Manin theory and elliptic F/V specializations. R07.6 imports this theorem for local applications, never supplies a backward prerequisite to R07.2.

Retain the full integral Fontaine-Laffaille construction and exactness/full-faithfulness/reduction results with unramified base and common shifted safe interval [0,p-2]. Keep rational filtration length < p distinct from torsion full faithfulness, and retain the separate restricted [0,p-1] endpoint statement and dyadic tests. Its R06.2 period-functor input is early; the later R06.4 comparison is a consumer, not a premise.

Retain Breuil-Kisin coefficient rings, Frobenius/Eisenstein height, classification functors, descent, generic-fibre and integral comparisons and the separately sourced p=2 theorem. Finite-flat, Barsotti-Tate, potentially Barsotti-Tate and unrestricted potentially semistable statements keep distinct hypotheses. Cohomological S-valued descent in AI.7 and deformation-ring component/image theorems are consumers, not replacement classifications or inputs.

Retain the extension-sensitive residual inertia and finite-flat calculations, ordinary/supersingular cases, peu/tres ramification and the dyadic versus odd-prime tests. Import the explicit R07.1 Raynaud/type input as well as R07.4. R15.4 owns the modular local-weight recipe and R20 its optimization; neither is a premise of these local calculations, and inertial semisimplification cannot discard the extension class.

FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeThe.keeps: Import the consolidated generic Grothendieck-Messing p-divisible/Hodge-filtration deformation equivalence from R07.2. Retain the additional source-specific tangent/obstruction computations using CR.0/CR.1 and DD.0/DD.1, and all local-condition stability, twisting, extension-of-fields, finite-flat model and generic-fibre comparisons. Apply A3 to actual abelian torsion and compare its Galois representation with the common arithmetic carrier. Preserve Fontaine finite-flat ramification and different bounds, including the shifted upper-numbering cutoff u > e*(n + 1/(p-1)), the translation G_Fontaine^(u) = G_standard^(u-1) to the unshifted convention and the different normalization v(p)=1. Keep every wild and p=2 hypothesis and proof; no conjectural higher-cohomology extrapolation is substituted for the finite-flat theorem. The general equivalence is imported, but each local application, compatibility square and numerical bound remains to be proved here.
FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeThe.reason: Consolidate the generic deformation proof at the earlier R07.2 target instead of duplicating it or creating R07.6 -> R07.2. All local deformation, ramification and abelian-torsion exports remain in R07.6, including its original A4 consumer.
